title: Why Salaried Taxpayers Should Wait to File ITR for FY26
description: The Income-Tax Department has released ITR forms for the Financial Year 2025-26 (Assessment Year 2026-27), but salaried taxpayers should exercise caution. It .

faq.q: Can I file my ITR before June 15 if my employer provides a provisional Form 16?
faq.a: It is strongly advised against filing with a provisional Form 16. Employers have until June 15 to issue the final Form 16, and provisional figures might change, leading to discrepancies and the need for a revised return.

faq.q: What is the Annual Information Statement (AIS) and why is it important?
faq.a: The AIS is a comprehensive statement available on the income tax portal that provides a consolidated view of all your financial transactions reported by various entities to the Income-Tax Department. It's important for cross-verifying your income and tax details to ensure accuracy before filing.

faq.q: What should I do if my Form 16 is delayed beyond June 15?
faq.a: If your employer delays issuing Form 16 beyond June 15, you should first follow up with them. If it's still not available, you can file your ITR using your payslips, bank statements, and Form 26AS, but ensure all calculations are accurate and match the TDS reflected in 26AS.

faq.q: What happens if there's a mismatch between my Form 16 and AIS/TIS?
faq.a: If you find a mismatch, you should first approach the reporting entity (e.g., your employer or bank) to get the discrepancy rectified. If it's an error in the AIS/TIS, you can submit feedback on the e-filing portal to correct the information. File your ITR only after resolution or with a clear understanding of the discrepancy.

faq.q: Is there a penalty for filing my ITR late?
faq.a: Yes, if you file your ITR after the due date (July 31 for individuals for FY26), a late filing fee under Section 234F is applicable. For income up to ₹5 lakhs, the fee is ₹1,000. For income above ₹5 lakhs, the fee is ₹5,000.

faq.q: Can I file a revised return if I make a mistake?
faq.a: Yes, you can file a revised return under Section 139(5) of the Income Tax Act if you discover any omission or wrong statement in your original return. The revised return must be filed before the end of the assessment year (March 31, 2027, for FY26) or before the completion of the assessment, whichever is earlier.
